parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
A sample of $\text{Al}$ reacts with an excess of $\text{Cl}_2$.

State the oxidation number of $\text{Al}$ in the product of the reaction.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State what determines the maximum oxidation number of the Period 3 elements in their oxides.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Separate samples of aluminium oxide, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, and phosphorus(V) oxide, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, react with an excess of $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ at room temperature.
parts.text: Give the state of $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ at room temperature.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Write an equation for the reaction of each oxide with an excess of $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ at room temperature.

$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + \ldots\ldots$$

$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: The oxide of silicon reacts with calcium oxide in an addition reaction to produce calcium silicate, $\text{CaSiO}_3$. The oxidation number of calcium in $\text{CaSiO}_3$ is $+\text{II}$.
parts.text: Deduce the oxidation number of silicon in calcium silicate.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Calcium oxide can be made from calcium carbonate in a single-step reaction.

Identify the type of reaction that occurs.
